"WELL YOU DID A SHIT JOB RAISING ME" - to my parents

It was a terrible thing to say, obviously. To be fair here, they didn't prepare me for the real world; they helicoptered me constantly and fed me sunshine and butterflies bullshit about people, especially women. They used guilt as a disciplinary weapon. What does that mean, you might ask? Well they basically would use guilt on me whenever I declared something for myself, or that I felt a certain way, or that I wanted something. They favored my sister, never believing anything I said.

I've moved past a lot of the negative conditioning I received as a kid - I never had it that bad, to be honest. We lived in a pretty normal suburb in a pretty normal house. I forgave my parents and I have a lot of opportunities today. The mental fuckery that resulted from all this left me without a healthy or positive mental road map, though. I wasted my high school and college years, and a promising athletic career at those levels. I've gone through OCD, depressions (some of them suicidal), and anxiety because I couldn't deal with things like a girl not being interested or feeling ashamed of myself for wanting anything in life. I read a great book called No More Mr. Nice Guy! that helped a ton. Overall, I wouldn't trade it. I was mentally fucked, and then I unfucked myself and in the process of doing so became much stronger physically and mentally.

I don't regret saying it, even though I know the damage it caused. I had to get it out. They weren't perfect - they were my parents and I love them to death, but I'm somewhat haunted by the person I could have been if I'd been confident, strong, and mentally solid from the beginning.
